api_checks.description: POST /auth/sign-out with a valid session cookie, then GET /links reusing that same (now-old) cookie: response is 401 — sign-out invalidates the session server-side so a subsequent authenticated request is rejected.

After POST /auth/sign-out, replay the identical original session-cookie value (i.e. do not rely on the client clearing/replacing the cookie) against GET /links: still 401, proving the session was revoked server-side (deleted/marked revoked_at in the session store) rather than merely relying on the client discarding it.

Call POST /auth/sign-out with no session cookie (or one already invalidated by a prior sign-out): response is 401 and no server state changes — no session row is created, mutated, or deleted as a side effect.
Authenticated POST /links with a safe (non-loopback, non-private, non-base-url) target: response is 201 and the returned code is at least 7 characters.

Authenticated POST /links with an unsafe target: response is 422. Also repeat for http://192.168.1.1/, http://10.0.0.1/, and a target whose host matches PUBLIC_BASE_URL — every one of these must independently return 422.

Authenticated POST /links with a target hostname that is not on any literal deny-list but would resolve via DNS to a loopback address (e.g. localtest.me -> 127.0.0.1): response is 201 (accepted), proving target_validation performs only literal scheme/host/IP-range string checks and never performs a DNS lookup or outbound network fetch to resolve/probe the host.

Issue a batch of authenticated POST /links calls with safe targets: every returned code is at least 7 characters drawn from a 62-character alphanumeric alphabet (>= 41.7 bits of entropy) and no two codes in the batch collide. (The `secrets`/`os.urandom` sourcing of the underlying bytes is verified at the unit layer by backend/tests/unit/test_code_generator.py, CHK-VM-011-unit — this api check is the runtime-observable half of VM-011.)
POST /links with no (or an invalid) session cookie: response is 401 and no link row is created.
With the database stopped/unreachable, GET /links (any non-/healthz endpoint) returns 503 with a JSON body carrying an `error` field.

With the database stopped/unreachable, inspect the 503 JSON body from GET /links and assert it contains no stack trace, no exception class name, and no filesystem path — only the safe `error` envelope.
After database reachability is restored, GET /healthz (and other endpoints) return to their normal, non-503 status — the 503 envelope does not persist once the database is reachable again.
